##### IS1. When rivers run low and hot: compound flash drought-heatwave stress on Tennessee Valley energy-water systems — Pursue

**Call.** UT Knoxville ISSE 2027 Seed Grants; RFP topics "modeling
sustainability and resilience under environmental stressors" and "extreme
hydrologic events ... for resilient energy-water systems".

**Team.** PI Yuefeng Hao (ISE). Co-PI Joshua S. Fu (Chancellor's Professor,
CEE; joint appointment in ORNL's Computational Earth Sciences Group) for
regional climate and extremes projections and climate impacts on energy
infrastructure ([CEE profile](https://cee.utk.edu/people/joshua-s-fu/)).
Co-PI Emine Fidan (Biosystems Engineering and Soil Science, UTIA; Hao as the
UTK PI meets the UTIA rule) for water availability and sectoral demand; a past
ISSE seed PI whose 2026 showcase was "Evaluating Water Availability and
Sectoral Demand for Sustainable Allocation"
([2025-2026 report](https://isse.utk.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/5/2026/11/ISSE-2025-2026-Annual-Report-compressed-2.pdf), p. 35).
Students: Yifan Gao (IS10 text task) and, from Spring 2027, Shi Jin. Partners
to invite: the PI's ORNL E3SM collaborators (Jiafu Mao, Xiaoying Shi, Yaoping
Wang), ORNL's regional-resilience initiative and TVA (river temperature, flow
and derate records, which need a data request); John Schwartz (TNWRRC) as
advisor. Nobody has been contacted; no partner has agreed to anything.

**Research question and approach.** Do compound flash drought-heatwave events
in the Tennessee Valley give a detectable land-surface signal (ET deficit,
soil-moisture drawdown, terrestrial-water-storage anomaly) weeks before the
river low-flow and high-temperature conditions that constrain river-cooled
generation, and how will their frequency change under E3SM-RRM and downscaled
projections? (1) An event catalog from multi-source remote sensing and drought
indices, merged with triple collocation. (2) Lagged links from those
indicators to USGS flow and temperature at intakes and to known TVA
curtailment periods. (3) Projected event frequency from Fu's downscaled
climate and ORNL's E3SM-RRM. (4) A screening map of which corridors with
announced large-load growth face the highest compound risk, reported as a
map, not as a siting decision. IS12 (reservoir "whiplash") can be an aim if
TVA data are available.

**Closest existing projects and papers, and the gap.** NSF Award API searches
for "flash drought" AND power, "thermoelectric" AND drought AND heat, "large
load" AND "extreme weather" and "Tennessee Valley" AND resilience returned no
awards ([example query](https://api.nsf.gov/services/v1/awards.json?keyword=%22data%20center%22%20AND%20flood)).
The closest NSF award, [2009726](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2009726)
(UNC, 2020), links drought and electricity systems to air-pollution exposure,
not to cooling-water constraints. TVA cut output at Browns Ferry in 2007, 2010
and 2011 because river temperatures were too high
([GAO-23-105375](https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-23-105375), search summary),
and TVA's adaptation plan names drought as a risk to river-cooled generation
([TVA 2022 CAP](https://www.sustainability.gov/pdfs/tva-2022-cap.pdf), search
summary): the hazard is documented, but not a land-surface early-warning
signal. ORNL's Southeast Resilience Accelerator works on heat, drought and
flood risk to Southeast energy infrastructure (search summaries of
[ORNL Regional Resilience](https://www.ornl.gov/regional-resilience/); page
403), so the gap claim against it is provisional. **Gap:** in the sources
checked, flash-drought onset science has not been tied to energy-water
operations in this basin. The thermoelectric water-vulnerability literature
was not re-checked.

**Novelty.** It moves flash-drought and heatwave hydrology from ecosystems
and agriculture to the thermal and low-flow limits of an energy system and
offers ORNL's resilience work a land-surface early-warning layer.

**Why us.** First-author papers on heatwave effects on CONUS hydrology
(*J. Hydrol.* 637, 2024) and flash-drought WUE and recovery (*AFM* 378, 2026);
first-author Priestley-Taylor and BMA ET algorithms (*AFM* 279, 2019);
co-author of triple-collocation drought-index integration (*SERRA* 36, 2022)
and the terrestrial-water-storage drivers paper (*J. Hydrol.* 635, 2024); Co-PI on the FFAR multi-source remote sensing flash
drought and flood tool; E3SM-RRM co-authorship and the DOE/ORNL grant (PI)
with ORNL modelers; the submitted paper on electricity-related water
consumption for projected data center load growth
([PI CV](../talent-pool/resources/hao-lab/Yuefeng_Hao_CV.md);
[hao-lab.md](../talent-pool/labs/hao-lab.md)).

**Fundability.** Mission fit with RFP topics 2 and 3; originality on energy
reliability and water; feasible in one year with existing data and ORNL
outputs; collaboration across ISE, CEE, UTIA, ORNL and TVA. Two external
targets: (1) DOE Office of Science BER through the FY2027 continuation
solicitation DE-FOA-0003665, tracked idea **B1**
([summaries/2026-10.md](summaries/2026-10.md)); the per-topic award size is not
stated, so the team sets the target amount after talking to the program
manager; submit before 2027-04-01 for FY2027 or use the seed results for
FY2028; odds are modest given the FY2027 budget request. (2) USGS Powell
Center working group, tracked idea **PC1** ([2026-11-22.md](2026-11-22.md));
the FY2028 call closes 2027-01-31, before the seed starts, so the FY2029 call
fits the seed timeline; the award is travel for up to 15 participants plus an
optional Fellow up to $100K. A fallback multi-investigator target is NSF BIO
**BE1** only if recast. CAREER **K1** cannot be a named target: it is
single-investigator, and ISSE requires multi-investigator follow-on proposals.

**Risks.** (a) Overlap with the current Hao seed, which names heat-wave
electricity demand and water: keep IS1 free of siting, noise, land markets and
the web tool, and say so in the narrative. (b) Overlap with the 104b TDEC grant
(from 2027-01): no facility withdrawal or thermal-discharge decision support.
(c) Overlap with the DOE Office of Science project the ISSE report lists (PI
Qiang He, co-PI Hao; "Water Availability and Flood Resilience in
Energy-Supporting Watersheds"): if active, frame IS1 as atmospheric and
land-surface compound-event science, not surface-groundwater modeling, and
list it as related support. (d) TVA data access is not secured. (e) Fourteen
days for CVs and signatures. (f) Six months of overlap with the current seed:
separate effort, and distinct tasks for Gao and Keating. (g) The open question
whether a current awardee may be PI again; if ISSE says no, move IS1 to Joshua
S. Fu as PI with Hao as co-PI.

**Verdict: Pursue,** as the single proposal with Hao as PI, after ISSE
confirms that a current seed holder may lead.

##### IS2. Will the grid hold? Transmission reliability of AI large-load growth in the Tennessee Valley under heat, drought and flood extremes — Pursue

**Call.** UT Knoxville ISSE 2027 Seed Grants; RFP topic "technologies related
to energy dominance and resilience" plus energy-water extremes.

**Team.** PI Kai Sun (Professor, EECS; CURENT member; EPRI project manager for
grid operations and planning 2007-2012; power system stability, control and
optimization; [EECS profile](https://eecs.utk.edu/people/kai-sun/)), who led
the ISSE hydrogen-transmission seed. Co-PI Yuefeng Hao (hydro-climate stress
scenarios and siting inputs). Optional co-PI: Leon M. Tolbert or Hector A.
Pulgar (both CURENT; registry). Students: Shi Jin (tariff- and
moratorium-aware siting model gives candidate load locations) and Yifan Gao
(queue-uncertainty model). Partners to invite: TVA; the ORNL Next-Generation
Data Centers Institute / GRID-C; CURENT; TDEC Office of Energy Programs. Kai
Sun has not been asked; IS2 needs Kai Sun's agreement to serve as PI. Nobody
has agreed to anything.

**Research question and approach.** How much AI data center load can the
TVA-region transmission system host at plausible sites while staying secure
during compound heat-wave demand peaks, derated river-cooled generation, and
voltage disturbances that make data center loads trip to backup power at
once? (1) Candidate load clusters from the students' siting models plus
announced projects. (2) Hydro-climate stress cases from the PI's heatwave and
flash-drought definitions (concurrent demand, derating and outage cases).
(3) Steady-state and dynamic studies on a synthetic or CURENT test-bed model
of the region, using Kai Sun's multi-timescale simulation methods. (4) Metrics:
hosting limits, ride-through and flexibility needs. IS7 (computer-vision asset
inventory) can be a data task.

**Closest existing projects and papers, and the gap.** NSF
[2610262](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2610262) (Lehigh,
2026, $518,881) studies cyber-physical stability of hyperscale data centers in
inverter-dominated grids, with no hydro-climate driver. EPCL large-load awards
[2603293](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2603293) and
[2541996](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2541996) cover
colocation energy management and flexible data centers in unit commitment.
NERC's incident review of the July 2024 Northern Virginia event (about 1,500 MW
of data center load lost at once after a 230 kV fault) is event analysis, not
a hydro-climate study
([NERC Incident Review](https://nerc.com/pa/rrm/ea/Documents/Incident_Review_Large_Load_Loss.pdf),
seen through search summaries; [APPA](https://www.publicpower.org/periodical/article/nerc-incident-review-examines-risks-challenges-tied-integration-large-loads)).
NSF Award API searches for "data center" AND flood returned no relevant award.
**Gap:** none of these combines load placement with compound hydro-climate
stress on a river-cooled fleet, the same gap tracked EPCL idea **P1** claims
([2026-11-22.md](2026-11-22.md)).

**Novelty.** Load location becomes a decision-relevant input to reliability
studies under hydro-climate stress; grid-side data center studies usually omit
hydro-climate stress, and hydro-climate studies usually omit grid dynamics.

**Why us.** The *RSER* 232 (2026) review of wildfire-power grid interactions
(with Fangxing Fran Li, Mingzhou Jin and Jiafu Mao); the heatwave and
flash-drought papers; two funded data center grants (ISSE footprint; 104b
TDEC); the submitted electricity-related water paper; Shi Jin's Tennessee
Valley siting model and substation digital-twin inspection experience; Yifan
Gao's queue-uncertainty siting model
([hao-lab.md](../talent-pool/labs/hao-lab.md)). Kai Sun's grid record comes
from the EECS profile and ISSE reports, not from the talent pool.

**Fundability.** Mission fit with energy resilience and energy-water
extremes; timely given NERC and FERC attention to large loads; feasible with
test-bed models and existing load lists; collaboration across EECS/CURENT,
ISE, TVA and ORNL. A non-awardee PI avoids the reapplication question. Two
external targets: (1) NSF ECCS EPCL (NSF 26-514, rolling), tracked idea
**P1**; recent EPCL large-load awards ran $200K-$585K, so about $500K over
three years is a team planning figure, not a sponsor figure. (2) NSF CMMI
core (NSF 26-515, rolling; 225-275 awards, $100M total) using the held idea
**C2** framing (data center-grid-water system-of-systems resilience), subject
to the partition rule in [summaries/2026-10.md](summaries/2026-10.md): if
**P1** or CAREER **K1** is pending, C2 cannot carry the same core. A TVA- or
EPRI-sponsored study is a possible third route, not checked.

**Risks.** (a) P1 and K1 partitioning ([2026-11-22.md](2026-11-22.md)).
(b) TVA's real network data are restricted, so a synthetic grid may be needed
(not checked). (c) The current Hao seed also names heat-wave electricity
demand: IS2 must be about transmission reliability, not where data centers
should go. (d) Kai Sun's interest and availability are unknown. (e) The 14-day
timeline.

**Verdict: Pursue,** with Kai Sun as PI; this is the safest structure. If only
one proposal is feasible in 14 days, submit IS2.

##### IS3. From forecast to mitigation: flood-robust protection and siting of energy-water assets in the Southern Appalachians — Revise

**Call.** UT Knoxville ISSE 2027 Seed Grants; RFP topic "flood preparedness,
and long-term mitigation strategies for resilient energy-water systems".

**Team.** PI Jon Hathaway (Professor, CEE; sustainable urban water and green
infrastructure; [CEE profile](https://cee.utk.edu/people/jon-hathaway/)), or
Haochen Li if ISSE confirms that a current awardee may lead. Co-PIs: Haochen

remote-sensing decision support) and optionally Kelsey Ellis (community
vulnerability). Partners: the City of Knoxville or KUB, TVA and TDEC. Nobody
has been contacted.

**Research question and approach.** Given high-resolution flood-hazard
ensembles, which long-term mitigation portfolio (elevate, harden, relocate,
add redundancy) for substations, water and wastewater plants and candidate
large-load sites minimizes expected service loss under deep uncertainty in
storm frequency? Exposure overlay on the Li engine's Helene hindcast and
design storms, then a two-stage robust or stochastic program; Shi Jin's
computer vision (IS7) supplies the asset inventory.

**Closest existing projects and papers, and the gap.** The Li seed does
forecasting for transportation and planning users
([ISSE news](https://isse.utk.edu/new-flood-forecasting-seed-project-targets-gaps-in-southern-appalachian-flood-risk-information/));
the Helene hindcast is published (Li, Hathaway and Canestrelli, *J. Hydrol.:
Regional Studies* 64, 2026, listed in the
[2025-2026 report](https://isse.utk.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/5/2026/11/ISSE-2025-2026-Annual-Report-compressed-2.pdf)).
The DOE Office of Science project the ISSE report lists (PI Qiang He) covers
"Flood Resilience in Energy-Supporting Watersheds" (scope not read). One search
found no peer-reviewed exposure study of Helene's effects on substations and
water plants, only news and utility accounts (e.g.,
[ENR on Asheville water repairs](https://www.enr.com/articles/59387-repairs-to-water-infrastructure-underway-after-hurricane-helene)).
**Gap:** the mitigation-decision layer; a thin claim, since the literature
check was one search.

**Novelty.** The step from flood forecasts to optimized long-term mitigation
of energy-water assets.

**Why us.** Co-PI on the FFAR flash drought and flood decision-support tool;
the ongoing stochastic optimization paper on irrigation planning under flash
drought and flood risks (with Mingzhou Jin and Brian Leib); robust siting
models by both students; the USGS 104b TDEC decision-support grant
([hao-lab.md](../talent-pool/labs/hao-lab.md)).

**Fundability.** A direct hit on RFP topic 3, but reviewers are funding the Li
seed now, and a second proposal from much of the same team could read as a
continuation. External targets if pursued: (1) NSF CMMI core (NSF 26-515)
with a disaster-resilience framing (not yet tracked; verify program fit);
(2) the TNWRRC USGS 104(b) FY2028 round, which can use TDEC Research
Priorities match (program tracked in [2026-11-19.md](2026-11-19.md); IS3 would
be a new idea and must stay off data center water to protect the 104b TDEC
grant).

**Risks.** (a) Overlap with the Li seed and the DOE Office of Science project.
(b) Hathaway and Li are committed to the Li seed. (c) A third Hao-involved
proposal spreads the lab thin. (d) The 14-day timeline.

**Verdict: Revise.** Raise it with Haochen Li and Jon Hathaway as a 2027
follow-on that their team leads; if they prefer to keep their seed's scope
clean, drop it for 2027.

## Ideas Overview

Research notes for this call are in [ideas/2026-11-25/](ideas/2026-11-25/)
([isse-seed-ideas.md](ideas/2026-11-25/isse-seed-ideas.md) and
[isse-seed-collaborators.md](ideas/2026-11-25/isse-seed-collaborators.md)).
"Why us" claims use only facts in
[talent-pool/labs/hao-lab.md](../talent-pool/labs/hao-lab.md) and
[talent-pool/resources/hao-lab/](../talent-pool/resources/hao-lab/).

### Summary of verdicts

| Call | Idea | Verdict | One-line why us |
|---|---|---|---|
| ISSE 2027 Seed Grants | IS1. Compound flash drought-heatwave stress on Tennessee Valley energy-water systems | Pursue (Hao as PI) | First-author heatwave-hydrology and flash-drought papers; triple-collocation and ET methods; FFAR flash drought tool; E3SM-RRM and DOE/ORNL ties |
| ISSE 2027 Seed Grants | IS2. Transmission reliability of AI large-load growth under hydro-climate extremes | Pursue (Kai Sun as PI, Hao as co-PI) | *RSER* wildfire-grid review; two funded data center grants; Shi Jin's Tennessee Valley siting model; Gao's queue-uncertainty model |
| ISSE 2027 Seed Grants | IS3. Flood-robust mitigation of energy-water assets in the Southern Appalachians | Revise (only if Haochen Li's team leads) | FFAR decision-support tool; stochastic optimization under flash drought and flood risk; students' robust siting models |
| ISSE 2027 Seed Grants | IS5, IS6, IS7, IS10, IS12 | Revise (IS7 into IS2 or IS3; IS10 and IS12 into IS1; IS5 and IS6 held) | Shi Jin's computer vision; Gao's NLP; poplar and bioeconomy thread |
| ISSE 2027 Seed Grants | IS4, IS8, IS9, IS11 | Drop | — |

### Which call should host which idea

- **ISSE hosts two proposals: IS1 (Hao as PI) and IS2 (Kai Sun as PI, Hao as
  co-PI).** The one-PI-per-researcher rule allows this. IS3 is a third,
  Li-led option only if Haochen Li and Jon Hathaway want it.
- **IS1 versus the current ISSE seed:** IS1 contains no siting, noise, land
  market or web tool; it is compound-event science for energy-water
  operations. **IS2 versus the current seed:** IS2 is transmission
  reliability, not where data centers should go. Students on the current seed
  (Gao, Keating) get distinct tasks during the six-month overlap.
- **IS1 and IS2 versus the 104b TDEC grant:** neither contains facility
  withdrawal or thermal-discharge decision support; IS3 stays off data center
  water.
- **IS3 versus Haochen Li's seed:** forecasting stays in the Li seed; IS3 adds
  only the mitigation-decision layer and must be led by that team.
- **External targets are unique per idea:** IS1 seeds DOE BER **B1** and USGS
  Powell **PC1** (FY2029 call); IS2 seeds NSF ECCS EPCL **P1** and NSF CMMI
  **C2**; IS3 targets a new CMMI disaster-resilience framing and a new 104(b)
  idea. **CAREER K1 cannot be a named target** (single-investigator; ISSE
  requires multi-investigator follow-on proposals).
- **IS2/P1 versus CAREER K1:** keep them apart as [2026-11-22.md](2026-11-22.md)
  requires (P1 is planner-side hosting limits; K1 is multi-decade siting and
  capacity). **C2:** under the [October summary](summaries/2026-10.md) rule,
  C2 cannot carry the same core while P1 or K1 is pending; do not have E1, C2
  and K1 pending at once with the same core.
- **IS1 versus PC1 and B1:** the seed supplies the event catalog and
  early-warning analysis; B1 keeps the E3SM-RRM compound-extreme runs and
  siting inputs, PC1 the national water-use synthesis.
- **IS1 and IS3 versus the DOE Office of Science project the ISSE report
  lists** (PI Qiang He, co-PI Hao): if it is active, IS1 stays on atmospheric
  and land-surface compound events, not surface-groundwater modeling, and IS3
  must show a distinct mitigation-decision scope; list the project as related
  support.
- **People:** Charles B. Sims, Jiafu Mao and Mingzhou Jin appear in several
  tracked calls; Kai Sun, Fu, Li, Hathaway and Fidan are recommended only
  here. Mingzhou Jin, as the ISSE director who receives proposals, is not
  listed as a team member in any idea. List the current ISSE seed, the 104b
  TDEC, FFAR and DOE/ORNL grants in every proposal.

### Open items and limits

- **For the user: check and update the resource files.** The
  [ISSE 2025-2026 Annual Report](https://isse.utk.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/5/2026/11/ISSE-2025-2026-Annual-Report-compressed-2.pdf)
  ("Sponsored Research", pp. 24-25) lists two sponsored projects with Hao as
  co-PI that are not in the talent pool files: DOE Office of Science
  "AI-Driven Coupled Surface-Groundwater Modeling for Water Availability and
  Flood Resilience in Energy-Supporting Watersheds" (PI Qiang He; co-PIs John
  Schwartz, Haochen Li and Yuefeng Hao; 2026-07-01 to 2027-03-31), and an NSF
  wildfire risk and WUI infrastructure resilience project, "Uncertainty-Aware
  and Cross-scale Modeling using Bayesian Inference for Wildfire Risk and
  Infrastructure Resilience in the Wildland-Urban Interface" (PI Jiafu Mao;
  co-PI Yuefeng Hao; 2026-02-01 to 2029-01-31). The same table shows four
  Hao-led proposals as active that the PI CV marks "Not Funded" (SE CASC
  compound drought-heat with cover crops; USDA NIFA topography and cover
  cropping; USDA NIFA "Digging Deeper"; BSF AI flash floods and flash
  droughts). **None of these was used in "why us".** The user should check
  them and update `talent-pool/resources/hao-lab/` if needed; the daily sync
  then carries any change into the lab summary.
- **Ask ISSE before 2026-12-09** whether a current seed holder may be PI
  again and whether budgets of consecutive seeds may overlap. If not, IS1
  moves to Joshua S. Fu as PI with Hao as co-PI.
- **IS2 needs Kai Sun's agreement as PI.** Kai Sun has not been asked; if Kai
  Sun declines, IS2 cannot go forward in this form (Hao's PI slot is reserved
  for IS1).
- **Timeline:** 14 days for teams, three-page narratives, CVs and all
  department-head signatures; start with IS2 if only one proposal is possible.
- **Unverified context:** the ORNL regional-resilience and ARMADA pages
  returned 403, so the accelerator's methods, data and contacts come only from
  search summaries; GAO-23-105375, the TVA CAP and the NERC incident review
  were seen through search summaries. Kate Evans's role in the accelerator is
  not confirmed.
- **Limited gap checks:** NSF Award API (loose keyword matching) and a few web
  searches; the thermoelectric water-vulnerability literature, Google Scholar,
  USAspending and DOE award lists were not queried for IS1-IS3. DOE BER and
  EPCL per-award amounts are not stated by the sponsors, so targeted amounts
  are planning choices.
- **Past winners:** award counts and amounts for 2024-2026, success rates,
  the review panel and repeat-PI policy are not published. Nicholas Shanahan
  (Li seed team) could not be identified.
- **Collaborators:** the profiles of Emine Fidan (search summary), John
  Schwartz (CEE page 404) and Hiba Baroud (not opened) are only partly
  verified. TVA data access, ORNL partnership and every named person's
  interest are unknown. Nobody has been contacted; none has agreed to
  anything.

### Considered but not listed

- ESIP Lab RFP "Connected Data: Interoperability, Discovery, and AI-Ready
  Access" ([RFP](https://www.esipfed.org/lab/rfp/); due 2026-12-14; $25,000
  total for 1-3 projects; 2027-02-01 to 08-01): verified this time (403 on
  2026-11-22), but the core topic is data infrastructure, not a lab
  direction; score 3.
- Natural Hazards Center Health and Extreme Weather Research Call 4 (rolling,
  $10K-$50K): needs perishable health data; score 3. Quick Response (up to
  $5K, social science): score 2.
- Below the relevance bar: NSF X-Labs "Computation at the Limit of Physics"
  (proposals reportedly 2027-02-08, not verified; score 2); NSF 27-501
  Foundational Research in Robotics (score 2); NOAA NCCOS coastal flood
  protection (2027-02-12; score 2); ASHRAE 1956-TRP compact CFD for data
  centers ($225K; 2026-12-15; score 2); TILOS AI Institute visitor program
  (travel only; score 3); EPA STAR air pollution and PFAS (off-topic).
- Framing only or not eligible: NSF DCL 26-023 (Genesis Mission; no money of
  its own); DOE Genesis Graduate Fellowship DE-FOA-0003673 (LOI passed,
  student-only); DOE LAB 27-3645 and LAB-27-3640 (national labs only);
  DHS-27-061-COE-SUPP (existing Centers of Excellence only); USGS CESU
  agreements (unrelated topics); TDEC Oak Ridge Reservation NRD restoration
  grants (restoration, not research); Midwest CASC small projects (Midwest
  tribal focus); APPA DEED and TN Grid Resilience (utilities only).
- Closed: NSF Energy-Water Security Initiative BAA (2026-08-06), DOE EFRC
  DE-FOA-0003614, CIEIF (2026-12-01, under 14 days), NAWI industrial reuse RFP
  (2026-11-24), NYSERDA (2026-12-02), UTRF maturation (2026-10-31), iHARP,
  Burroughs Wellcome climate and health, IEEE PES wildfire RFP; UT-ORII StART
  no longer active; UT Grand Challenges on other topics; Microsoft AI Economy
  Institute, Google academic awards (quantum only), Cisco, Meta, Colorado and
  Texas water boards (not open or not eligible).
- Not posted yet: DOE Genesis Mission FY27 Phase I (DE-FOA-0003612 has only a
  2026-12-17 Phase II deadline for FY26 awardees), NOAA NIDIS FY2027, USDA
  NIFA AFRI FY2027, NRCS CIG FY2027 (connection reset), NEUP FY2027 (403),

- No open call: SE, South Central and Northeast CASCs; external seed calls at

# Funding Calls — Scan 2026-11-28

New funding calls found in this scan with strong relevance to Hao Lab, per the
"Funding Call Scan Rule" in [CLAUDE.md](../CLAUDE.md). Each call appears in only
one scan file; see [seen-calls.md](seen-calls.md) for the full index.
Directions come from the lab summaries in [talent-pool](../talent-pool/README.md).

> Last scanned: 2026-11-28

**Verification note (2026-11-28):** all three search tracks were run:
(1) federal programs (Grants.gov API: every opportunity posted in the last 7
and 30 days, all forecasts from research agencies, and about 70 keywords;
DOE Office of Science Open FOAs and DOE eXCHANGE; NSF announcements, DCLs and
BAAs; NIFA, drought.gov and NASA SARA pages); (2) sub-award and seed programs
of funded centers and networks (watch-list items, NSF research networks and
community facilities, NASA- and USDA-linked centers, NOAA-linked programs,
resilience centers, NSF IUCRCs and Engines, Southeast consortia); and
(3) societies, foundations, industry, international and state programs
(Water Research Foundation portal, NCEAS, NAWI, Schmidt Sciences, UKRI, BARD,
Wellcome, Future Earth, FFAR, Google.org, Microsoft, EPRI, insurance and
actuarial research funders, Southeast regional bodies). Official pages were
opened with curl. Pages that could not be verified: waterrf.org (bot check),
NAS Gulf Research Program (403), EPRI award PDF (404/500), AmeriFlux community
page (403), cpo.noaa.gov funding page (blocked), GAIN/INL (bot check),
dhs.gov long-range BAA topics (403), NSPIRES and simpler.grants.gov search
(script-loaded), Schmidt Sciences and NAWI InfoReady lists (script-loaded),
Willis Research Network (429), Quadrature (connection reset). The UT Knoxville
limited-submissions URL now redirects to a general researcher-resources page.

## New Calls

No new calls qualified in this scan (strong Hao Lab relevance, eligible,
next deadline on or after 2026-12-12 or rolling, and verified on an official
page). No ideas or collaborator recommendations were generated, because the
Funding Idea Rule and the Collaborator Rule apply only to new calls.

| Next Deadline | Sponsor | Program | Award Size | Hao Lab Fit (score) | Suggested Team | Link | Added |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

### Watch list (re-checked today; report when posted)

- **NIH/NIEHS Health and Extreme Weather Solutions-Focused Research Hubs
  (RFA-ES-28-002, U54)** and the companion data center (RFA-ES-28-003): still
  "forecasted" on Grants.gov (last updated 2026-06-26); the estimated posting
  date of 2026-11-27 passed without a posting, and the NIH Guide URL returns
  "Page not found". Forecast terms: application about 2027-01-29, ceiling
  $2,000,000, 6 awards. Even if posted, it is a public-health hub needing
  health partners, so Hao Lab could lead at most an exposure component.
- **DOE Genesis Mission FY27 Phase I:** not posted. DE-FOA-0003612 still has
  only the 2026-12-17 Phase II deadline for FY26 Phase I awardees.
- **DOE eXCHANGE items marked "Not Published":** DE-FOA-0003642 FASTER
  (Frontier Advancement in Scalable Technologies for Energy Resilience) and
  DE-FOA-0003643 STRONG-DS (next-generation distribution systems); report if
  published.
- **NOAA NIDIS FY2027 Coping with Drought, USDA NIFA AFRI FY2027, NASA
  ROSES-26/27:** not posted.
- **NCEAS Morpho working groups:** "Next Morpho Call for Proposals coming
  February 2027".
- **LTER Network 2027 SPARC competition:** announced, no RFP or dates yet.
- **NSF IUCRC:** not accepting proposals; NSF expects an updated solicitation.
- **NAWI Regional Water Solutions RFP:** not yet posted (RFI closed
  2026-09-09).
- **Southeastern Sun Grant FY2027 RFA, BRIDGES Engine (TN/AL) and Grid
  Modernization Engine (Carolinas) R&D calls, Schmidt Sciences VICC next
  call, Southern SARE R&E 2027, SE CASC consortium call:** not posted.

  for Water and Wastewater Utilities"). The portal label "Upcoming Grant" is
  stale; WRF's announcement (mirrored on wateronline.com, 2025-09-23) shows
  the batch closed 2025-11-20. The next likely entry point is WRF's
  Unsolicited Research Program pre-proposal call (last announced January
  2026; inference, not a verified date).

### Considered but not listed

- **WRF RFP 5463** "Assessment of Reclaimed Effluent for Non-Evaporative
  Cooling in Data Centers" and **5457** "Watershed and Wildfire Drivers of
  Water Quality" ($200,000 each, due 2026-12-31): invitation only (WRF
  roster). **5449** "Data Center Wastewater and Biological Treatment":

- **USGS CESU agreements after 2026-12-12** (G27AS00090, 00063, 00041,

  Corridors**: score 1. **EPA OASES NOFOs** (air pollution, PFAS): off-topic.
- **Southern Extension Risk Management Education Center 2027 NOFO**
  (closed 2026-11-12) and **Southern SARE On-Farm Research** (closed
  2026-11-13).
- **Membership consortia** (ES2 IUCRC, Purdue Grid of Tomorrow, MIT Data
  Center Power Forum, EPRI DCFlex): projects chosen by paying members; no
  open call for non-members. **EPRI University Global Research Award**: no
  round after 2025.
- **TDOT research** (biennial cycle closed), **Appalachian Regional
  Commission** (no open RFPs), **Sea Grant** (Tennessee has no program;
  MS-AL and GA calls in-state or closed), **DOE BER Southeast US FOA**
  (DE-FOA-0003420, closed 2024).
- **Other universities' internal seed programs** with deadlines from

### New Calls

| Next Deadline | Sponsor | Program | Award Size | Hao Lab Fit (score) | Suggested Team | Link | Added |

| 2026-11-12 (federal; TN institute internal deadline is earlier) | USGS | Water Resources Research Act National Competitive Grants FY2026 (104g General), G27AS00164 | Up to $120K; ~4 awards; 1:1 non-federal match | Data center water use (2.1); 5 | Yuefeng Hao, Yifan Gao, Shi Jin | [Grants.gov](https://simpler.grants.gov/opportunity/2c5fcf26-2264-42ae-9bc9-60f591fd770c) | 2026-10-21 |
| Pre-application suggested by 2026-11-30; applications by 2026-12-01 for FY2027 funding; closes 2027-09-30 | DOE Office of Science | FY 2027 Continuation of Solicitation for the Office of Science Financial Assistance Program, DE-FOA-0003665 (BER) | Not stated per topic | Earth system modeling & ecosystem vulnerability (2.3); 4 | Yuefeng Hao (+ ORNL collaborators) | [DOE SC](https://science.osti.gov/grants/FOAs/FOAs/2027/DE-FOA-0003665) | 2026-10-21 |
| Rolling (proposals accepted anytime) | NSF GEO | Geosciences Core Research (GEO Core), NSF 26-516, Earth Sciences program | ~200-350 awards; ~$110M total | Climate extremes & ecohydrology (2.2); 5 | Yuefeng Hao, Shi Jin | [NSF](https://www.nsf.gov/funding/opportunities/geo-core-geosciences-core-research-atmospheric-geospace-earth-ocean/nsf26-516/solicitation) | 2026-10-21 |
| Rolling (proposals accepted anytime) | NSF ENG / CBET | Energy, Water, and Resource Engineering (EWRE), under NSF 26-518 | Not stated | Data center energy-water footprint (2.1); 4 | Yuefeng Hao, Yifan Gao | [NSF](https://www.nsf.gov/funding/opportunities/energy-water-resource-engineering) | 2026-10-21 |
| Rolling (proposals accepted anytime) | NSF ENG / CMMI | CMMI core programs, NSF 26-515 (Advanced Manufacturing, Design, and Operations; Engineering for the Built Environment) | Not stated | Data center siting optimization under uncertainty (2.1, 2.4); 4 | Yifan Gao, Shi Jin, Yuefeng Hao | [NSF](https://www.nsf.gov/funding/opportunities/engineering-eng-civil-mechanical-manufacturing-innovation/nsf26-515/solicitation) | 2026-10-21 |
| 2027-07-28 | NSF | Faculty Early Career Development Program (CAREER), NSF 22-586 | Not stated | PI eligibility (Assistant Professor since 2026-08), any lab direction; 5 | Yuefeng Hao (sole PI; no co-PIs allowed) | [NSF](https://www.nsf.gov/funding/opportunities/career-faculty-early-career-development-program) | 2026-10-21 |

#### Call Notes

**USGS 104g General FY2026 (G27AS00164)** — the most urgent and best-matched call.
- The FY2026 general competition targets data center water use: observing,
  estimating, validating, and forecasting water use by data centers and other
  water-intensive industries (withdrawals, cooling demand, local impacts), with
  AI/ML methods encouraged.
- Fits Hao Lab's ISSE data center footprint project and the USGS 104b TDEC
  decision-support grant; Yifan Gao and Shi Jin's siting models supply the
  demand side.
- Only State Water Resources Research Institutes submit to Grants.gov.
  Tennessee applicants go through the Tennessee Water Resources Research
  Center (tnwrrc.tennessee.edu), whose internal deadline was not found and
  will be before 2026-11-12. Contact the center immediately.
- 1:1 non-federal cost share required; up to 3-year projects; anticipated start
  2027-05-01.

##### Ideas: USGS 104g General FY2026 (G27AS00164)

**Key call facts.** The call closes **2026-11-12, 5:00 PM ET**, and only the State Water Resources Research Institute submits. In Tennessee that is TNWRRC, whose internal deadline was not found and will be earlier. The maximum award is **$120,000**, with about 4 awards expected out of $462,500 in program funds. At least $1 of non-federal match is required per federal dollar, met in each 12-month budget period. Federal funds cannot pay indirect costs, and the PI's federal salary is capped at 2 months per year ([Grants.gov](https://simpler.grants.gov/opportunity/2c5fcf26-2264-42ae-9bc9-60f591fd770c); [NOFO](https://files.simpler.grants.gov/opportunities/2c5fcf26-2264-42ae-9bc9-60f591fd770c/attachments/1931b7a5-8a2e-4007-a158-cbf31be312cd/Foa_Content_of_G27AS00164_100226.pdf)). The topic is narrow: "observing, estimating, and validating water use associated with data centers and other industries drawing from public supply systems," including forecasting future usage. AI/ML is "a central requirement" ([NOFO p.5](https://files.simpler.grants.gov/opportunities/2c5fcf26-2264-42ae-9bc9-60f591fd770c/attachments/1931b7a5-8a2e-4007-a158-cbf31be312cd/Foa_Content_of_G27AS00164_100226.pdf)). Scoring gives **20 of 100 points to Executive/Secretarial Order alignment** (SO3444 on AI, EO14303 Gold Standard Science, EO14239 local preparedness). A **USGS letter of support is required**, signed by center leadership. The anticipated period is 2027-05-01 to 2030-04-30.

The most important external fact is a USGS Water Mission Area project on data center water use. Its posting says it covers direct, site-level (Scope 1) cooling water and "does not address indirect water use associated with data center energy demands (Scope 2 use)", and that it uses NLP over the literature and utility filings ([Zintellect DOI-USGS-2026-33](https://www.zintellect.com/Opportunity/Details/DOI-USGS-2026-33)). That project is both the duplication risk and the natural partner for the required letter.

**Recommendation: submit one merged proposal, "Observe–Estimate–Forecast: an AI framework for data center water use in Tennessee."** Aim 1 is the observing layer (U3 + U4), Aim 2 is validated estimation (U1), and Aim 3 is forecasting under extremes and policy (U2).

###### U1. Tennessee data center water use: hybrid physics-ML estimation validated against independent records — Pursue (merged lead)

**Team:** Yuefeng Hao (PI), Yifan Gao, Shi Jin; Mingzhou Jin as a possible collaborator (UT ISE/ISSE, listed in hao-lab.md; participation not confirmed).

**Research question and approach.** Can Scope 1 water use (direct use from public supply and self-supply) of Tennessee data centers be estimated at the facility or county level with calibrated uncertainty, from public and utility data? Can Scope 2 (thermoelectric water tied to their electricity) be attributed on top of that? The model chain is a hybrid physics-ML estimator: IT load → cooling technology → water-use effectiveness, plus grid mix → plant-level water intensity. It produces probabilistic outputs and is validated on 3–5 Tennessee facilities with utility or permit data obtained through letters of support.

**Closest existing work and gap.** Siddik, Shehabi and Marston (2021) gave the first spatially detailed US water footprint of data centers ([LBNL](https://eta-publications.lbl.gov/bibcite/reference/34978)). The Ren group works at national and peak-capacity scale ([arXiv 2304.03271](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.03271v4); [arXiv 2603.02705](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.02705)). Minnesota Sea Grant funds a facility-level real-time estimation dashboard for Minnesota ([MN Sea Grant](https://seagrant.umn.edu/research/ai-water-impact)). The USGS project above covers Scope 1 only. None found does ML-based, uncertainty-quantified, validated Scope 1+2 estimation for one balancing authority (TVA).

**Novelty.** Methods are incremental, but geography and validation are strong. The project also directly fills the Scope 2 gap that USGS's own project leaves open.

**Why us.** The PI holds the ISSE grant on the local water footprint of AI data centers in Tennessee and the USGS 104b TDEC grant on data center and SMR withdrawals. The PI also has a submitted paper, "Regional screening of electricity-related water consumption for projected data-center load growth" (with Kaylee Jin, *Water Resources and Industry*, under review), which is the direct precursor for Scope 2. Gao's and Jin's ongoing Tennessee Valley siting papers supply the demand side.

**Fundability.** It hits "estimating, validating, forecasting", the AI/ML requirement and "validating results against independent or ground truth data" almost verbatim. Training points (10) are covered by naming Gao and Jin as federally supported students.

**Risks.** Ground-truth access (utility billing at MLGW, KUB and others) is unconfirmed. Whether Tennessee withdrawal registration data are accessible was not verified. $120K over 3 years is a small budget. The program screens for overlap with the 104b project, so the proposal must say plainly that 104b produces a TDEC decision tool while 104g produces validated estimation methods.

**Verdict: Pursue.** Lead with Scope 1 from public supply, as the NOFO frames it, and present Scope 2 as the "associated" component that complements the USGS project.

###### U2. Seasonal, heatwave and flash-drought forecasts of data center water demand under siting-policy scenarios — Pursue (Aim 3 of U1)

**Team:** Yuefeng Hao, Yifan Gao, Shi Jin.

**Research question and approach.** How do weather-driven peak cooling demand and flash-drought or heatwave stress on source water combine with policy-aware build-out (tariffs, moratoria, interconnection queues) to shape future demand on Tennessee public supply?

**Closest existing work and gap.** "Small Bottle, Big Pipe" projects national peak-day capacity needs of 697–1,451 MGD through 2030 ([arXiv 2603.02705](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.02705)). "AI Data Centers and the Water Use Feedback Loop" finds burdens of 0.2%–134% of host capacity across ten sites ([arXiv 2606.21760](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.21760)). An ACS study finds about 25% of 9,347 data centers face water stress at least one month a year ([ACS](https://www.acs.org/pressroom/presspacs/2026/october/many-data-centers-are-located-where-water-resources-are-limited.html)). None couples policy-aware siting scenarios with process-based flash-drought and heatwave hydrology at local supply scale.

**Novelty.** Real. It joins three things no one has joined.

**Why us.** The PI's papers on heatwave effects on CONUS hydrology (*J. Hydrol.* 2024) and on flash-drought ecosystem effects and recovery. Shi Jin's "Siting Under Moving Rules" (tariff- and moratorium-aware siting in the Tennessee Valley) and Yifan Gao's robust siting under interconnection-queue uncertainty.

**Fundability.** It answers "forecast future scenarios" and "seasonal variability", and supports EO14239 local preparedness.

**Risks.** Forecasts cannot be validated within the award, and on its own the idea reads as planning. That is why it is an aim of U1, not a standalone proposal.

**Verdict: Pursue as Aim 3 of U1.**

###### U3. Computer-vision detection of data center cooling technology — Revise (Aim 1 data layer)

**Team:** Shi Jin, Yuefeng Hao.

**Approach and change.** The original idea, quantifying evaporative loss from Landsat, ECOSTRESS or MODIS thermal and ET signals, is physically weak. Cooling towers are building-scale. ECOSTRESS is 70 m, ET algorithms are calibrated for vegetation, and its industrial use so far is detecting once-through thermal plumes ([ECOSTRESS poster](https://ecostress.jpl.nasa.gov/downloads/other/ECOSTRESS_aquatic_applications_poster.pdf)). The revised version classifies cooling technology (wet towers, dry or adiabatic coolers, chillers) from high-resolution imagery, following WRI's satellite method for power plants. That method reached 90% precision on cooling type and 69% on water demand across 200 US plants ([WRI](https://www.wri.org/research/methodology-estimate-water-demand-thermal-power-plants-data-scarce-regions-using-satellite)). Thermal anomalies serve only as signals of operating status.

**Gap.** No satellite or aerial detection of data center cooling type was found.

**Why us.** Shi Jin's YOLO/EfficientNet inspection models and SLAM-based infrared + LiDAR registration for a substation digital twin; the PI's MODIS and multi-source remote sensing work. Shi Jin starts in Spring 2027, so this aim should be scheduled from year 1, semester 2.

**Verdict: Revise.** Use it as the "observing" input to U1, not as a standalone proposal.

###### U4. Provenance-tracked disclosure dataset with an AI bias audit — Revise (Aim 1 data layer)

**Team:** Yifan Gao, Shi Jin.

**Approach and change.** Extract water-use statements from permits, utility filings and sustainability reports into a source-linked dataset, then audit it for bias and inconsistency. This matches the NOFO's "enhance data transparency, improve traceability, and identify sources of bias" almost word for word. However, the USGS project already runs NLP over the literature and utility filings ([Zintellect](https://www.zintellect.com/Opportunity/Details/DOI-USGS-2026-33)), and corporate disclosures are voluntary and not comparable ([AIhub/The Conversation](https://aihub.org/2025/09/24/data-centers-consume-massive-amounts-of-water-companies-rarely-tell-the-public-exactly-how-much)).

**Why us.** Gao's undergraduate NLP and information-extraction work and the planned source-linked dataset of data center requirements; Jin's 350K-paper ETL and retrieval platform.

**Verdict: Revise.** Offer the Tennessee dataset to the USGS team as a complement. This strengthens the "integration with USGS science" element instead of competing with USGS.

###### U5. SMR + data center withdrawals and thermal discharges — Drop

This idea nearly repeats the funded 104b TDEC project. No SMR–data center pair is operating in Tennessee to observe (none found), and reactor cooling is outside the call's focus on public supply. Cite 104b as the decision-support pathway (information transfer) and as evidence of past performance.

**DOE Office of Science FY2027 continuation (DE-FOA-0003665)**
- Umbrella solicitation covering all Office of Science programs, including
  Biological and Environmental Research (BER). Fits the PI's E3SM / CIVE
  ecosystem-vulnerability work with ORNL.
- A pre-application is required for some review panels; check Part 1 and the
  BER topic list for an Earth and Environmental Systems Sciences topic before
  writing.

##### Ideas: DOE Office of Science FY2027 continuation (DE-FOA-0003665), BER

**Key call facts.** The FY2027 BER panels with fixed dates cover only Microbial Biosystems Design, Bioimaging and Sensing, and Low Dose Radiation. Their pre-applications are due 2026-12-22 and full applications 2027-03-16 ([NOFO Part 1](https://science.osti.gov/-/media/grants/pdf/foas/2027/DE-FOA-0003665-Part-1.pdf)). This differs from the 2026-11-30 / 2026-12-01 dates in the 2026-10-21 scan file, which came from search results. Earth-system work goes in as an **off-panel application "at any time" within BER's mission**, which includes "energy-relevant... human system processes." Narratives over 15 pages may be declined. Applications received after April 1 may roll into the next fiscal year ([NOFO](https://science.osti.gov/-/media/grants/pdf/foas/2027/DE-FOA-0003665-Part-1.pdf)).

The decisive constraint is budget. The FY2027 request zeroes Environmental System Sciences and Atmospheric System Research, cuts Earth and Environmental Systems Modeling from **$118.5M to $29.0M**, and says the remaining Earth-system work will use AI-enhanced, coupled models "to enhance weeks to years predictive skill for energy expansion" in "target regions... particularly sensitive to... water availability." It also says ESS "completes most research on permafrost, boreal ecology" ([FY2027 BER budget request](https://www.energy.gov/documents/fy-2027-biological-and-environmental-research-budget-request)). A House bill reportedly restores BER to about $800M ([CRS R48944](https://www.congress.gov/crs-product/R48944); summary only). An April 2026 BER Dear Colleague Letter invited regional centers on severe weather hazards to energy infrastructure, up to $5M each, with Daniel Winkler as contact ([BER DCL](https://science.osti.gov/-/media/ber/pdf/Funding/2026/BER-Dear-Colleague-Letter.pdf)). The odds are modest and depend on appropriations. Contact a BER program manager before writing.

###### B1. Water availability for Tennessee Valley energy expansion under compound flash drought-heat extremes: AI-enhanced E3SM-RRM coupled to large-load siting — Pursue

**Team:** Yuefeng Hao (PI); ORNL collaborators listed in hao-lab.md (Jiafu Mao, Xiaoying Shi, Yaoping Wang, Daniel M. Ricciuto, Peter E. Thornton, Forrest M. Hoffman; participation and funding mechanism to be confirmed); Yifan Gao and Shi Jin for the large-load use case.

**Research question and approach.** Do compound flash drought-heat events in the Tennessee Valley cut summer cooling-water availability on weeks-to-months timescales in ways that siting assumptions based on annual or HUC2 averages miss? There are four work packages: (1) E3SM-RRM/ELM compound-extreme runs over the Southeast; (2) ET, T/ET and WUE recovery constraints from AmeriFlux and BMA-merged ET products; (3) a drought-regime surrogate for large ensembles (B2); and (4) sub-basin, seasonal water availability and cooling-water stress as inputs to data center and SMR siting.

**Closest existing work and gap.** PNNL's BER-funded IM3/GCAM-USA work covers data center water at state or HUC2 scale, focused on the West ([OSTI 2998851](https://www.osti.gov/dataexplorer/biblio/dataset/2998851); [OSTI 2589826](https://www.osti.gov/dataexplorer/biblio/dataset/2589826)). Alston, Love and Haider model data center energy and water for Michigan ([arXiv 2609.25437](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.25437)). E3SMv2's North American RRM was built "to inform the US energy sector about changes in water availability... heat waves" ([Tang et al., GMD 2023](https://gmd.copernicus.org/articles/16/3953/2023/)), but no Southeastern compound flash drought-heat application was found. None found couples ESM drought projections to large-load siting.

**Novelty.** Real, provided the hypothesis is about Earth-system predictability and optimization is the use case.

**Why us.** The PI is a co-author on the submitted overview of the E3SMv3 regionally refined configuration (*JAMES*, under review). The PI is lead author of CIVE v1.0 (*Ecological Indicators*, second revision) and PI of the DOE/ORNL vulnerability grant ($229,835, 5 years). The PI is also PI of the 104b TDEC data center + SMR water grant and the ISSE footprint grant, and leads two students who are building Tennessee Valley siting models. No other team found holds all of these.

**Fundability.** It mirrors the budget request's "target regions," "water availability for energy," "multi-sector dynamics" and "AI surrogate components." Program policy factors include "PI not previously supported by SC"; whether a lab subcontract counts as SC support is unknown.

**Verdict: Pursue.** Send a one-page concept to a BER EESM program manager first, keep the narrative to 15 pages or fewer, and submit before 2027-04-01.

###### B2. Regime-aware AI surrogate of E3SM land drought response and recovery — Revise

**Team:** Yuefeng Hao, Shi Jin, Yifan Gao, with ORNL collaborators.

**Approach and gap.** E3SM land-model surrogates already exist for methane, GPP-SIF, groundwater and fire ([Chen et al., JAMES 2023](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1029/2022MS003135); [GMD 2022](https://gmd.copernicus.org/articles/15/1899/2022/)), and E3SM has released a flagship emulator 100 times faster than earlier capabilities ([FY2027 BER request](https://www.energy.gov/documents/fy-2027-biological-and-environmental-research-budget-request)). No drought- or recovery-specific emulator was found. The documented biases point in opposite directions. ORNL's publication record of the PI's flash-drought paper describes ELMv2 as prolonging GPP recovery after flash drought ([ORNL record](https://impact.ornl.gov/en/publications/evaluating-ecosystem-water-use-efficiency-and-recovery-dynamics-d/); external description, not a talent-pool fact). Multi-model studies find drought legacies about 4 times too short ([Kolus et al., Sci. Rep. 2019](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-019-39373-1)). A surrogate that depends on drought regime, constrained by flux observations, would address both.

**Why us (partial).** The PI's paper "Evaluating ecosystem water use efficiency and recovery dynamics during flash droughts: insights from observations and model simulations" (*Agricultural and Forest Meteorology* 378, 110982, 2026, with ORNL co-authors) and the PI's AGU 2024 talk on flash-drought recovery and WUE at the Missouri Ozark AmeriFlux site. The lab has no emulator publications. Shi Jin lists Earth system models only as an interest.

**Verdict: Revise.** Use it as B1's AI component, or as a standalone only if ORNL co-investigators lead the emulator architecture and Hao Lab leads the observational constraints and the decision use.

Keep it as a seed or a fallback if BER says siting is out of scope. **Why us:** the PI's E3SMv3 RRM co-authorship, CIVE v1.0 lead authorship, and heatwave hydrology paper.

Fold it into B1 as validation, or move the science to GEO Core (G1).

It overlaps the PI's active DOE/ORNL grant, "Quantification of Boreal and Temperate Ecosystem Vulnerabilities and Their Model Uncertainties," and the budget request says BER is completing boreal ecology research. Use that grant's results as preliminary data for B1.

Decision-support framing fits poorly. This is the one call where data centers should not appear.

The field is crowded on onset and forecasting: Land-Atmosphere Interactions in Flash Drought Development ([NSF 2414601](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2414601)), Otkin/Gerken on land-atmosphere feedbacks ([NSF 2303458](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2303458)), the Auburn CAREER ([NSF 2144293](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2144293)), the 2026 CAIG AI awards ([NSF 2616279](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2616279), [NSF 2702406](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2702406)) and DroughtRx ([NSF 2544077](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2544077)). **Recovery** in humid forests is much less funded. The two closest recovery awards study deep root-zone water in Texas ([NSF 2549574](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2549574)) and aquatic carbon during Southeastern watershed reconnection ([NSF 2627600](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2627600)).

###### G1. Beyond soil-moisture recovery: thresholds, transpiration shifts and lagged carbon-water recovery after flash drought in humid Southeastern ecosystems — Pursue

**Team:** Yuefeng Hao (PI); ORNL E3SM collaborators (to be confirmed); a new hydrology graduate student to be budgeted. Gao and Jin work on siting and should not be counted as hydrology personnel. Shi Jin could contribute a scientifically justified ML sub-aim for detecting regime shifts.

**Research question and approach.** H1: humid forests cross from energy-limited to water-limited ET only briefly, and the threshold shifts under concurrent heat (high VPD). H2: T/ET rises under heat during onset and stays perturbed after soil moisture recovers. H3: GPP and ET recovery lag soil-moisture recovery, with the lag set by VPD and refill of deep storage. H4: E3SM's land model reproduces recovery timing only when VPD-stomatal and deep-water processes are represented. Methods: AmeriFlux flux towers plus multi-source remote sensing; an ensemble of Priestley–Taylor and complementary-relationship models merged by BMA to quantify structural ET uncertainty during extremes; benchmarking with ORNL.

**Closest existing work and gap.** Zhang et al. analyzed 151 FLUXNET flash-drought events and found that WUE rises during recovery in forests but not in croplands ([HESS 2020](https://hess.copernicus.org/articles/24/5579/2020/)). Flash droughts with extreme heat recover more slowly ([Nature Geoscience 2025](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41561-025-01719-y)). A soil-moisture threshold controls coupling during drought-heatwaves ([Commun. Earth Environ. 2025](https://www.nature.com/articles/s43247-025-02977-9)). Stoy's award partitions ET across the US but not specifically during compound extremes ([NSF 2422397](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2422397)). No funded project tests whether recovery follows soil moisture in humid Southeastern forests against ESM process representation.

**Novelty.** It tests a paradigm, which matches the solicitation's "transformative" language. Without the recovery and humid-regime framing, it would overlap 2414601 and 2303458.

**Why us.** The PI's flash-drought WUE and recovery paper (*AFM* 2026) and AGU 2024 Missouri Ozark AmeriFlux talk; the heatwave hydrology paper (*J. Hydrol.* 2024); drought-recovery papers (*J. Hydrol.* 2023, China and Korea); the ET-model portfolio (soil-water-index Priestley–Taylor, *AFM* 2019; complementary relationship + BMA, *AFM* 2019; BMA drivers of ET, *J. Hydrol.* 2022; conductance-based ET partitioning, *J. Hydrol.* 2021); and ORNL E3SM collaborators. Few NSF-funded flash-drought groups pair observed recovery diagnostics with an ESM team.

**Fundability.** It is foundational critical-zone and land-atmosphere science, produces a public event-recovery dataset (a stated measure of success), and benefits from the early-career priority.

**Risks.** Southeastern flux-tower coverage of the 2016 and 2019 flash droughts was not checked. The PI's ISE affiliation may raise questions in EAR, which the hydrology publication record answers. PT, CR and BMA may look like legacy methods unless tied to hypotheses.

**Verdict: Pursue.** Email a one-page summary to WaLCZ@nsf.gov and ask about typical award size.

###### G2. Does flash drought reach the deep critical zone? Vertical propagation into root-zone, groundwater and terrestrial water storage — Revise

**Change.** Replace "TWS in flash vs. conventional drought" with a hypothesis about propagation and legacy: does a surface deficit lasting weeks reach deep storage, and does storage memory predict the recovery lags in G1? The method combines GRACE/GRACE-FO with root-zone soil moisture and well data to bridge the weeks-vs-months scale gap.

**Gap.** A 2025 RSE paper maps global flash-drought hotspots from daily reconstructed GRACE ([RSE 2025](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0034425725002974)) but does not study propagation mechanisms. The NSF API returned no TWS-plus-drought award.

**Why us.** The PI's co-authorship on long-term terrestrial water storage change (*J. Hydrol.* 2024, with ORNL) and the drought-recovery papers.

**Risks.** GRACE resolution and finding groundwater data.

**Verdict: Revise.** Make it Aim 3 of G1 or a second proposal after G1.

###### G3. Soil-moisture thresholds for post-flash-drought carbon recovery and rewetting pulses — Revise (aim of G1)

Limit it to CO2 (NEE, GPP and Reco from flux towers) and test whether the ESM represents Birch-type rewetting pulses. hao-lab.md lists no chamber or GHG field capacity, so CH4 and N2O come in only with a measuring partner (none identified). The evidence on pulses conflicts: grassland rewetting gives N2O and CO2 pulses ([Science Advances](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/sciadv.abb7118)), while a meta-analysis finds +35.7% CO2 with no significant N2O effect ([PMC9871208](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9871208/)). **Why us:** the PI's *npj Climate and Atmospheric Science* 2025 review on soil moisture controls over carbon sequestration and GHG emissions, and topic lead of the RUBISCO Soil Moisture Working Group mini-workshops. Ask the program officer whether EAR or BIO/DEB is the right home.

###### G4. AI/computer-vision flash-drought detection — Drop

This collides with the two 2026 CAIG awards, DroughtRx, the Auburn CAREER and a fast-growing CNN, GAN and U-Net literature ([Foroumandi et al., WRR 2024](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1029/2023WR035600)). The lab has no published geoscience AI work. Keep ML only as a G1 sub-aim for detecting regime shifts.

##### Ideas: NSF CBET EWRE (NSF 26-518)

**Key call facts.** EWRE "supports fundamental research to advance energy, water, and resource management," including "AI modeling that incorporate[s] novel metrics" and "closing energy, water and resource loops." It sends Earth-system science to GEO and "buildings and cities" to CMMI. Contact is **cbet-ewre@nsf.gov**, and a one-page summary to the program director is strongly encouraged ([EWRE program page](https://www.nsf.gov/funding/opportunities/energy-water-resource-engineering); [NSF 26-518](https://www.nsf.gov/funding/opportunities/engineering-eng-chemical-bioengineering-energy-transport/nsf26-518/solicitation)). No award size is stated. A sample of 41 recent standard awards coded EnvS/EWRE had a median of about **$393K** ([NSF API](https://api.nsf.gov/services/v1/awards.json?keyword=optimization&fundProgramName=EnvS-Environmtl%20Sustainability&dateStart=01/01/2024)). No EWRE-coded award mentioned data centers. Data center water work at NSF sits in CISE DESC ([NSF 2324916](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2324916)).

###### E1. Drought- and heat-robust co-design of data center cooling technology, water sourcing and operations with grid-attributed water — Pursue

**Team:** Yuefeng Hao (PI), Yifan Gao, Shi Jin; Mingzhou Jin as possible optimization collaborator (not confirmed); a thermal-engineering Co-PI is needed (none in the talent pool).

**Research question and approach.** For a fixed set of candidate Tennessee Valley sites, which mix of cooling technologies (evaporative, hybrid or adiabatic, dry, liquid) and water sources minimizes a new **drought-conditioned, stress-weighted total (direct + indirect) water** metric at acceptable cost and reliability? The model is a two-stage distributionally robust optimization. Stage 1 chooses cooling portfolio and water source; stage 2 chooses hourly wet/dry switching and load flexibility. Ambiguity sets come from compound flash-drought and heatwave scenarios. Indirect water is decision-dependent: the cooling choice changes grid load, and indirect water is attributed at generator level across the TVA/SERC fleet, including derating at river-temperature limits. Following the cross-call partition, regional siting and capacity expansion stay in CAREER K1. E3 (reclaimed water) is an aim here, and E2 (SMR) is a case-study module.

**Closest existing work and gap.** Vabson et al. site data centers by county with a deterministic base model ([arXiv 2601.16315](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.16315)). Xiao, You et al. analyze national scenarios, estimating 731–1,125 million m³/yr for AI servers ([Nature Sustainability](https://re.public.polimi.it/retrieve/536a055b-d8ab-4b86-bd4d-88facfaaf2ae/s41893-025-01681-y.pdf)). "Balancing Bits and Drops" uses static county-month AWARE stress factors to evaluate, not optimize ([arXiv 2607.22617](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22617)). Alston et al. found that air cooling halves total water but raises indirect water by a third in Michigan, but they assess rather than optimize ([arXiv 2609.25437](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.25437)). None treats cooling choice as a decision that moves water between the site and the grid under drought-heat uncertainty.

**Novelty.** Decision-dependent indirect water under hydro-climate ambiguity, plus a new metric. This is a methods contribution, not a relabeling.

**Why us.** The PI's flash-drought and heatwave science supplies the uncertainty model. The PI's submitted electricity-related water screening paper supplies the grid-water attribution base. Gao's robust siting and Jin's tariff-aware Tennessee Valley models supply the optimization base. The ISSE and 104b grants supply data access and a state-agency stakeholder.

**Fundability.** It matches "AI modeling... novel metrics," the early-career priority and "novel connections across scientific domains." A 3-year budget of about $400K fits the observed norm.

**Risks.** The program director may route it to CMMI (operations research) or to CBET Transport Phenomena (cooling hardware). Keep water-resource limits (withdrawal and consumption caps, basin depletion, thermal limits) at the core. Credible cooling performance curves need a thermal Co-PI. The PI's submitted paper may overlap Alston et al. and must be distinguished from it.

**Verdict: Pursue.** Send a one-page summary to cbet-ewre@nsf.gov stressing water-resource management, and run a targeted Scopus search ("distributionally robust" + "data center" + "water") before writing.

###### E2. Withdrawal and thermal-discharge management for SMR-co-located data center campuses under river-temperature extremes — Revise (module of E1)

**Gap.** SMR–data center studies cover economics and grid stability, not water ([arXiv 2608.10999](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10999); [arXiv 2603.09110](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.09110)). The constraint binds in this region: TVA derated or shut down Browns Ferry units when the river exceeded 90 °F, and the 2010 event reportedly cost nearly $50M ([SEJ](https://www.em.sej.org/headlines/hot-river-forces-costly-cutback-tva); [APR 2007](https://www.apr.org/2007-08-17/heat-and-drought-shut-down-tva-reactor)).

**Why us.** The 104b TDEC grant covers exactly this combination, and research direction 2.1 names SMR co-location.

**Risks.** That same closeness is the overlap risk with 104b. hao-lab.md lists no reactor thermal-hydraulics or plume expertise.

**Verdict: Revise.** Make it a case study inside E1 unless a nuclear or thermal Co-PI joins. If it ever stands alone, it must contribute foundational methods well beyond the 1-year TDEC deliverable.

###### E3. Circular water sourcing: reclaimed-water networks for data center clusters under drought — Revise (aim of E1)

**Why us.** Facility-location and network optimization (Gao, Jin) plus drought hydrology (Hao).

**Risks.** Treatment-quality constraints need an environmental-engineering partner (none in the talent pool), and Tennessee effluent data were not found.

##### Ideas: NSF CMMI core programs (NSF 26-515)

**Key call facts.** NSF 26-515 (posted 2026-08-17) combines AMDO, EBE, IIDS and MAMS. Proposals are accepted anytime, with 225–275 awards and $100M expected, and no PI limits. Proposers are strongly encouraged to send a one-page summary to the program director ([NSF 26-515](https://www.nsf.gov/funding/opportunities/engineering-eng-civil-mechanical-manufacturing-innovation/nsf26-515/solicitation)). **EBE** covers infrastructure "systems-of-systems" for "water, energy, and other essential services" under "hazards, extreme events, and cascading effects" (cmmi-ebe@nsf.gov) ([EBE page](https://www.nsf.gov/funding/opportunities/ebe-engineering-built-environment)). **AMDO** emphasizes manufacturing but supports "new analytical methods to aid decision-making in the design and operation of... systems" (cmmi-amdo@nsf.gov) ([AMDO page](https://www.nsf.gov/funding/opportunities/amdo-advanced-manufacturing-design-operations)). Comparable recent single-PI awards run about $330K–$520K over 3 years ([NSF 2534745](https://api.nsf.gov/services/v1/awards/2534745.json); [NSF 2611922](https://api.nsf.gov/services/v1/awards/2611922.json)). Former Operations Engineering work was still being funded under legacy codes into late 2026.

###### C1. Siting AI data centers under endogenous rules (AMDO) — Pursue after program-director email

**Team:** Yifan Gao, Shi Jin, Yuefeng Hao; Mingzhou Jin as the only listed optimization collaborator (Co-PI role not confirmed).

**Research question and approach.** How should a planner site and expand capacity when (i) the chance of a moratorium or tariff change in a jurisdiction rises with the MW already sited and water already withdrawn there, spreading spatially; (ii) interconnection-queue information is revealed only by entering the queue; and (iii) substation and basin water headroom tighten with the planner's own decisions? The model class is multistage stochastic or distributionally robust programs with decision-dependent feasible regions. Contributions are decomposition, cuts and bounds on the value of modeling endogeneity, with an empirical hazard model fitted to moratorium and opposition data. C3 is one thrust, and the Tennessee Valley is the testbed.

**Closest existing work and gap.** Data center siting under queue delays treats delay as an exogenous scenario ([Abdelhady et al., ESCAPE 2026](https://psecommunity.org/wp-content/plugins/wpor/includes/file/2606/LAPSE-2026.0251-1v1.pdf); [Shao et al., arXiv 2510.25118](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.25118); [Kim et al., Nat. Commun. 2026](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-026-72324-9)). Decision-dependent facility location makes demand endogenous, not the feasible set ([Başçiftçi et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1912.05577); [Pantuso 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.09816); [NSF 2534745](https://api.nsf.gov/services/v1/awards/2534745.json)). Stakeholder-approval constraints are static ([NSF 2620205](https://api.nsf.gov/services/v1/awards/2620205.json)). The motivation is strong: at least 75 projects worth about $130B were blocked or delayed in Q1 2026, and statewide moratorium bills appeared in 14 states ([Data Center Watch](https://datacenterwatch.org/q1-2026)).

**Novelty.** Genuinely methodological. No facility-location model with a spatially contagious, decision-dependent regulatory hazard was found (web search only).

**Why us.** Both student papers provide the base models: Gao's robust siting under queue uncertainty and Jin's tariff- and moratorium-aware Tennessee Valley siting. Gao's NLP background can build the event data. The ISSE grant measures the noise, water and land-market drivers of local acceptance.

**Fundability.** It fits AMDO's "analytical methods to aid decision-making" with AI. It is not manufacturing, so the program director must confirm fit.

**Risks.** The team has a thin OR-theory record. The PI's 15 papers are in hydrology, climate and energy reviews, and both students are new. The hazard is hard to identify from few events. Strong theory groups (Minnesota, Pantuso) are competitors. Mitigate with preliminary computational results from the two student papers.

**Verdict: Pursue after a program-director email.** Submit after at least one student paper is out.

###### C2. Compound heat-drought resilience of the data center-grid-water system-of-systems (EBE) — Revise (hold)

**Team:** Yuefeng Hao, Yifan Gao, Shi Jin; a power-systems Co-PI is needed (none in the talent pool).

**Approach.** A coupled hydro-thermal-electric model in which heat raises cooling load while cutting generator and cooling-water capacity. It adds a compound flash drought-heatwave event generator, resilience metrics, and design for adaptability (siting, cooling mix, water sourcing).

**Gap.** Interdependent-infrastructure resilience awards leave out data centers and drought or heat ([NSF 2541220](https://api.nsf.gov/services/v1/awards/2541220.json)). Data center-grid awards are about electrical or cyber risk ([NSF 2613408](https://api.nsf.gov/services/v1/awards/2613408.json)). Water-utility drought awards leave out data centers ([NSF 2622226](https://api.nsf.gov/services/v1/awards/2622226.json)).

**Why us.** This is the strongest combination in the pool. It draws on the PI's heatwave, flash-drought and wildfire–power grid publications (*RSER* 2026), the 104b and ISSE grants, the ORNL E3SM link, and the students' siting models.

**Why hold.** Its research core is nearly the same as CAREER K1 and overlaps EWRE E1. Submit it only if the CAREER route is closed or program officers advise EBE over CAREER. In either case, do not have it pending at the same time as K1.

###### C3. Text-to-constraint uncertainty for infrastructure decisions — Revise (thrust of C1)

**Approach.** Turn calibrated NLP/LLM rule-extraction error into chance constraints or ambiguity sets over constraint structure, with guarantees on decision quality as a function of extraction accuracy.

**Gap.** LLM ordinance extraction exists for wind and solar, at 85–90% accuracy for NREL's wind database ([NREL](https://research-hub.nrel.gov/en/publications/supporting-energy-policy-research-with-large-language-models-a-ca/)). No data center ordinance database, and no optimization model that propagates extraction error, was found.

**Why us.** Gao's NLP and information-extraction work and the planned dataset of data center requirements; Jin's ETL and retrieval platform.

**Verdict: Revise.** It stands alone only if a targeted prior-art search confirms the gap. Otherwise fold it into C1.

Neur2SP and Neur2RO already cover learned surrogates for facility location ([arXiv 2205.12006](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2205.12006); [arXiv 2310.04345](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.04345)), and CMMI funded the JHU group's foundations of ML and discrete optimization in 2026 ([NSF 2550265](https://api.nsf.gov/services/v1/awards/2550265.json)). Both are absorbed into C1 as computational enablers.

###### K1. Siting AI computing infrastructure under hydro-climate extremes: robust planning of coupled compute-power-cooling-water systems (ENG/CMMI-EBE) — Pursue

**Team:** Yuefeng Hao (sole PI). Students Yifan Gao and Shi Jin. Collaborators by single-sentence letters only: ORNL (E3SM scenarios) and Mingzhou Jin (optimization mentoring); none confirmed.

**Research question and approach.** How should multi-decade siting and capacity plans for data centers and co-located power account for nonstationary, spatially correlated compound extremes (heat-drought, low flow) that shrink cooling water and tighten thermal-discharge limits across a shared basin and grid at the same time? There are three thrusts. (i) Generate extreme scenarios from observations, remote sensing and E3SM-class projections. (ii) Build correlated-hazard robust or distributionally robust siting and capacity models with withdrawal and thermal-discharge constraints, extending the Gao and Jin models. (iii) Model moving policy constraints as uncertainty. Thrust (iii) must stay light so it does not duplicate AMDO C1.

**Education.** A "siting under extremes" data-science studio in IE 465/565 Applied Data Science; AI-for-infrastructure cases in IE 591; statistics-of-extremes modules in IE 200. The policy activity is the TDEC decision outputs.

**Closest existing work and gap.** Data center CAREER awards are all operational ([NSF 2541996](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2541996), [NSF 2544321](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2544321), [NSF 2340042](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2340042), [NSF 2045641](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2045641)). Energy-water CAREER precedents predate AI data centers ([NSF 1845931](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=1845931), [NSF 1847404](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=1847404)). Existing siting tools are screening indices ([PESGM 2026](https://index.mirasmart.com/PESGM2026/PDFfiles/PESGM2026-001928.pdf)) or colocation economics ([NSF 2603293](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2603293)). No NSF-funded project that treats hydro-climate extremes as the uncertainty in data center siting was found. That is a statement about NSF awards, not proof that no paper exists.

**Novelty.** Foundational methods for siting interdependent compute-power-water infrastructure under spatially correlated hydro-climate extremes.

**Why us.** The PI has published on flash drought, heatwaves, ET and terrestrial water storage, and is also PI of two data center water grants in one basin (104b TDEC, ISSE). The PI has an ORNL E3SM collaboration, supervises two students already writing Tennessee Valley siting papers, and teaches the three courses the education plan uses.

**Fundability.** It is an integrated research-education plan in an ENG program whose scope ("water, energy... extreme events, cascading effects") fits almost verbatim, and it supports a budget of $500K or more.

**Risks.** Eligibility is unconfirmed. The optimization record is mostly the students' unpublished papers, so get at least one siting paper submitted before July 2027. Reviewers may read it as a Tennessee case study, so lead with the method. It must be distinguished from 104b, ISSE and EWRE E1. The field is fast-moving.

**Verdict: Pursue.** Confirm eligibility with the Department Head first, then email the EBE and EWRE program contacts to choose between K1 and K2.

###### K2. Drought-conditioned water accounting and planning for the AI compute build-out (ENG/CBET-EWRE) — Revise (alternate framing of K1)

**Approach.** Basin-level, drought-conditioned water footprints of compute and power demand, building on the PI's submitted electricity-related water paper and replacing static stress factors with dynamic ones driven by ET and soil moisture.

**Gap.** SCARF and "Balancing Bits and Drops" use static stress factors for operations ([arXiv 2506.22773](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.22773v2); [arXiv 2607.22617](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22617)).

**Verdict: Revise.** Only one CAREER is allowed per year. Choose K1 or K2 after program-officer feedback. If EWRE E1 is already pending, K2 is too close to it and K1 is the right choice.

###### K3. Forecast-informed stochastic water allocation under flash drought — Revise (backup)

**Gap.** Flash-drought detection and decision-scale forecasting are saturated at NSF: DroughtRx, a $938,299 CAREER ([NSF 2544077](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2544077)), the Tian CAREER ([NSF 2144293](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2144293)), CAIG ([NSF 2616279](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2616279)) and CHIRRP ([NSF 2435046](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2435046)). Only a decision-science contribution in ENG (multistage allocation under probabilistic onset forecasts) is open.

**Why us.** FFAR flash-drought decision-support tool (Co-PI) and the ongoing paper "A Decision-Support Model for Irrigation Planning under Flash Drought and Flood Risks Using Remote Sensing and Stochastic Optimization" (Rui Xi, Hao, Leib, M. Jin).

**Risk.** Reviewers may see it as continuing FFAR, where the PI is not lead.

**Verdict: Backup** if K1 and K2 are judged out of scope.

###### K4. Tennessee Valley AI footprint observatory — Drop (and generic energy-water optimization — absorbed)

An observatory reads as monitoring, its noise and land-market parts fit SBE better than ENG, and it duplicates the ISSE grant. Its remote-sensing and data layers go into K1's education and broader impacts. A generic "optimization under uncertainty for energy-water transitions" theme lacks a hook against existing nexus CAREER awards. Its methods engine and the SMR angle (no NSF award mentioning small modular reactors was found since 2019) are absorbed into K1.
